title: Kobi <> Taryn: Weekly Planning - 2026/08/10 10:30 EDT - Notes by Gemini
screen_reason: Jumpr-internal 1:1 that includes WagerTech delivery content: status of client document feedback, partial sandbox access, board reconciliation and handover, ticket drafting quality, and the PRD as a build basis.

items.statement: Kobi said he is behind on following up on the feedback and comments the client contact (Chester) left in various documents, and that the team meets the client the next day (2026-08-11).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I I've caught up with Chester earlier today and I'm still behind on following up with a lot of their uh feedback and comments that they left in various documents. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I'm going to try to get caught up now that there's you know we we're meeting them tomorrow and there's that uh looming pressure.
items.asr_note: The transcript does not name the project at this line. Attribution to WagerTech comes from the next passages (WagerTech partial sandbox at L277-281) and from Jira (WAGR-82 quotes Kobi: 'let me check with Chester'). Chester may be an ASR rendering of a client contact name [ASR?].

items.topic: Process client feedback; assign items to Taryn
items.statement: Kobi will work through the outstanding client feedback today and, where he finds suitable items, assign them to Taryn to work on in Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I'm going to work through that today and then if uh if I do see some things that I can assign over to you to work in the meantime, um I'm going to uh I'll send them your way so that uh you can start working through in Salesforce as well.

items.topic: Taryn has own partial sandbox user
items.statement: Taryn confirmed she has access to the WagerTech partial sandbox with her own user account, which was set up the previous week. Kobi noted she switches between a rep account and the partial sandbox admin account when testing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um that said, like did you were you able to get access to the partial sandbox with like your own account / Kobi Kunasekaran: uh that just set up last week? / Taryn Reithofer: Yes. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I would recommend like especially because like you know you're you're switching between like a rep account / Kobi Kunasekaran: versus um by our partial sandbox um admin account.
items.asr_note: Sandbox identified as WagerTech at L277 ('widget techch partial SP' = WagerTech partial SB [ASR?]) and L281 ('partial SP wager tag' = WagerTech [ASR?]).

items.topic: Clean up and reconcile WagerTech board
items.statement: Kobi will go through the WagerTech board today to clean it up and reconcile it, because many tickets have already been worked, and see what remains.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, so yeah, I'll go through the board today. I'm going to try to get get that cleaned up. I know this has worked through quite a bit of tickets already, so um need to reconcile and uh see if there's anything else left.
items.asr_note: 'this has worked through' may be a misheard name of the person who worked the tickets [ASR?]. Board identified as WagerTech at L332-339.

items.topic: Taryn to take over WagerTech board
items.statement: Kobi said WagerTech is the more pressing board because it is in active implementation with many moving parts. He proposed that Taryn work toward taking over the board this week or next so he can focus on the build and implementation. No firm handover date was set.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'll try to sign some things over to you and then I think maybe by like this week or next week we'll work towards like uh work towards you being able to like take over the board as well / Kobi Kunasekaran: um we can we can do that next afterwards. Uh I think wet tech is more uh more pressing since it we're actively implementing. There's a lot of uh moving parts. So, um if if you can take over the board and and some of those things and I can just focus on the build um and the implementation and we can actually get through this / Taryn Reithofer: Yeah. Okay.

items.statement: Kobi said many newer WagerTech tickets were drafted with Claude. The build numbers in them help, but early tickets (e.g. build 8) carry more source detail than needed and later ones (builds 54, 60) carry too little information.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh it's a mix of Claude and me going through, but yeah, like a lot of the a lot of the newer tickets um I've worked with Claude to kind of work through. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I actually like the fact that it adds like the build number and everything. That's been actually helpful. But in the ticket itself like sometimes it leaves like more information about like the source of the uh the story than it actually needs to be there. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And like if you look at anything like after like I'm looking through like build 54 60 like those ones, they're much smaller. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like there's too little information in those.
items.asr_note: Build numbers are heard as 'build eight' (L355, Taryn) and 'build 54 60' (L360); mapping to BUILD-n ticket labels is an inference.

items.statement: Taryn suggested Kobi draft tickets first and then use Claude to make them more robust. Kobi said this might be the way to go. No firm change was agreed.
items.quote: Taryn Reithofer: Maybe you start and then get Claude to make it more robust if that makes sense. / Kobi Kunasekaran: potentially, yeah. Yeah, I think that that might be the way to go.
items.supersedes_hint: Implied change from Claude-first ticket generation used on WagerTech (L400) to manual-first drafting; only proposed.

items.topic: PRD-based POC fields questioned by client
items.statement: Kobi said the initial POC was built from the client's PRD, and the client then questioned many of the fields in it, although those fields came from the PRD. He said the PRD is not an accurate source to build from.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean, we we've already like learned the lesson. Like we the initial like PC and everything that we built based off of all the PRD um there was so many things that were like why is this here? I'm like it's a new PRD like you wanted it there. We got we got got all of these fields from your PRD. / Kobi Kunasekaran: We can't just assume that we're going to be able to guess the right ones because already we've established that the PRD isn't necessarily the most accurate information to go off of.
items.asr_note: 'PC' = POC [ASR?]; 'a new PRD' likely 'in your PRD' [ASR?]

items.statement: Kobi said that, instead of inferring requirements from the PRD, he now pushes back and asks the client to state exactly what changes they want; Jumpr will make changes once they are specified. This is Kobi's stated internal stance; client acceptance is not shown in this meeting.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So So like because of that like now I've just been pushing back and like / Kobi Kunasekaran: okay tell me exactly what you want. like this is we built this based on the information we got. Um if you need changes, happy to make the changes, but I need to know what what those are.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier build basis was the client PRD (initial POC); now changes require explicit client specification.

gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Taryn Reithofer: Maybe you start and then get Claude to make it more robust if that makes sense. / Kobi Kunasekaran: potentially, yeah. Yeah, I think that that might be the way to go.
